title: Pushes and Pulls
bigQuestion: What makes things start, stop and change the way they go?

story.title: Who Is Pushing? Who Is Pulling?
story.kicker: Come to the playground. Look close. Someone is pushing. Someone is pulling.
paragraphs: It is recess at a school in Chicago. The playground is full. Ana sits on a swing. Her friend Leo stands behind her. Leo pushes the swing. Ana flies up. She comes back down. Leo pushes again.
Over by the fence, Sam has a wagon. It is full of balls. Sam grabs the handle. He pulls. The wagon rolls along. It bumps over a crack. Sam pulls harder. The wagon keeps going.
Near the slide, a soccer ball sits still. Mia runs up. She kicks it. The ball zooms across the grass. It hits the wall. It bounces back. Now it rolls the other way.
Look around. Every moving thing got a push or a pull. The swing. The wagon. The ball. Nothing started moving on its own. Somebody made it move.
story.think: Pick one thing on your playground. Who pushes it? Who pulls it?

lessons.title: A Push Makes It Go
lessons.mainIdea: A push moves a thing away from you.
reading: A ball sits on the floor. It does not move. It waits. Then you push it. Your hand moves it away from you. Now the ball rolls. Your push made it go.
A *push* is a *force*. A force is what makes things move. When you push, you press on a thing. You move it away from you. A push can be small. A push can be big.
Look for pushes. You push a door open. You push a cart. You push a button. You push off the wall in a pool. Pushes are everywhere.

words.d: to press on a thing and move it away from you

look.title: The Shopping Cart
look.text: Look at the cart in the store. It is empty. It sits still. A girl puts her hands on the handle. She pushes. The cart rolls down the aisle. She pushes more. It goes faster.
look.prompt: What made the cart start to move?

check.q: What made the ball roll?
check.why: The ball sat still until a hand pushed it. The push made it go.

check.q: Which one is a push?
check.why: Pressing the door moves it away from you. That is a push. Dragging and tugging are pulls.

check.q: A push moves a thing which way?
check.why: When you push, you press on a thing. It moves away from you.

lessons.title: A Pull Makes It Come
lessons.mainIdea: A pull moves a thing toward you.
reading: A wagon sits on the grass. You grab the handle. You pull. The wagon comes toward you. It rolls along behind you. Your pull made it go.
A *pull* is a force too. When you pull, you tug on a thing. You move it toward you. You pull a rope. You pull a zipper. You pull a dog on a leash.
A push and a pull are both forces. A push sends a thing away. A pull brings a thing closer. Both can start a thing moving.

words.d: to tug on a thing and move it toward you

look.title: Tug of War
look.text: Two teams hold one long rope. Each team pulls. The rope moves a little this way. Then a little that way. Then the red team pulls harder. The rope slides toward the red team. The blue team slides too!
look.prompt: Why did the rope move toward the red team?

check.q: Which one is a pull?
check.why: Tugging the handle brings the wagon toward you. That is a pull.

check.q: A pull moves a thing which way?
check.why: When you pull, you tug on a thing. It comes toward you.

check.q: What do a push and a pull both do?
choices: They both send a thing away
They both bring a thing closer
They both can start a thing moving
check.why: A push and a pull are both forces. Both can make a still thing start to move.

lessons.title: Making It Stop
lessons.mainIdea: A push or a pull can stop a moving thing.
reading: A ball rolls toward you. You put out your hands. The ball hits your hands. Your hands push back. The ball stops. A push stopped it.
A moving thing keeps going. It needs a force to *stop*. A wall can push on a ball. The grass rubs on a ball. Your hands can catch a ball. Each one is a push that makes the ball stop.
Pulls can stop things too. A dog runs. The leash goes tight. The leash pulls the dog. The dog stops.

words.d: to end moving and hold still

look.title: The Rolling Ball
look.text: A ball rolls across the gym floor. It goes and goes. Then it rolls onto the thick mat. The mat rubs on it. The ball slows down. It stops. It never rolls far on the mat.
look.prompt: Why did the ball stop on the mat?

check.q: What stops a rolling ball?
choices: Only the color of the ball
check.why: A moving thing needs a force to stop. Hands, a wall or grass can push on it.

check.q: The leash goes tight. What happens to the running dog?
choices: The dog keeps running the same way
check.why: The tight leash pulls on the dog. The pull stops the dog.

check.q: You catch a ball. What do your hands do?
choices: Pull the ball to go faster
Push on the ball to stop it
check.why: Your hands push back on the ball. That push makes it stop.

lessons.title: Big Push, Little Push
lessons.mainIdea: A bigger push makes a bigger change.
reading: Tap a toy car. It rolls a little. It stops fast. Now push the car hard. It zooms across the room. It goes far. The big push made a big change.
A small push makes a small change. A big push makes a big change. The same is true for pulls. Pull a wagon gently. It creeps. Pull it hard. It jumps forward.
Try it. Roll a ball with a soft push. Mark where it stops. Roll it with a hard push. Mark again. Which mark is farther? That is your *evidence*.

words.d: what you see or measure that shows an idea is true

look.title: Two Kicks
look.text: Jae kicks a ball softly. It rolls to the cone. Then Jae kicks the same ball hard. It rolls past the cone. It rolls past the tree. It rolls all the way to the fence.
look.prompt: Which kick was bigger? How do you know?

check.q: You want the car to go far. What should you do?
check.why: A big push makes a big change. The hard push sends the car far.

check.q: A soft push makes what kind of change?
check.why: A small push makes a small change. The car moves only a little.

check.q: Jae's ball rolled to the fence. What does that show?
check.why: The ball went far. A big push makes a big change. So the kick was hard.

lessons.title: Changing Direction
lessons.mainIdea: A push or a pull can change which way a thing goes.
reading: A ball rolls to the left. You tap it with your foot. Now it rolls to the right. Your push changed its *direction*. Direction is the way a thing goes.
Kick a ball at a wall. The wall pushes back. The ball bounces off. It comes back a new way. A push can turn a moving thing.
Pulls turn things too. A kite flies straight. You pull the string. The kite swoops to the side. The pull changed its direction.

words.d: the way a thing is going

look.title: Ball on the Wall
look.text: Look at the ball. It rolls straight at the wall. Bump! It hits the wall. Now it rolls back toward you. The ball did not roll through the wall. The wall pushed it back.
look.prompt: What changed the direction of the ball?

check.q: What is direction?
choices: The way a thing is going
check.why: Direction is the way a thing goes, like left or right.

check.q: A ball hits a wall and bounces back. What did the wall do?
choices: It pushed the ball a new way
It made the ball stop for good
check.why: The wall pushed back on the ball. The push sent it a new direction.

check.q: You pull a kite string. What can happen?
check.why: A pull can turn a moving thing. The kite swoops to the side.

lessons.title: Ball Meets Ball
lessons.mainIdea: Things that touch can push each other.
reading: A blue ball sits still. A red ball rolls at it. Bump! The red ball pushes the blue ball. The blue ball starts to roll. The red ball slows down.
Balls that *touch* can push each other. Blocks can push each other too. So can toy cars. When two things bump, each one pushes the other.
You can plan a bump. Roll a marble at a block. The block moves. Aim well. You can knock down a tower with one marble.

words.d: to bump into or press on another thing

look.title: The Bowling Ball
look.text: Look at the pins. They stand in a row. A bowling ball rolls down the lane. It hits the first pin. That pin falls into the next pin. That pin falls too. Soon they are all down.
look.prompt: What pushed the last pin? It never touched the ball.

check.q: The red ball rolls into the blue ball. What happens?
choices: The blue ball starts to move
check.why: The red ball pushes the blue ball when they touch. The push makes it roll.

check.q: When two balls bump, which one pushes?
check.why: When two things bump, each one pushes the other. The red ball slows down too.

check.q: The bowling ball hits one pin. How do the other pins fall?
choices: Each pin pushes the next one
check.why: Each falling pin touches the next pin and pushes it over.

lessons.title: Ramps and Heavy Boxes
lessons.mainIdea: A push can solve a problem, like moving a heavy box.
reading: A big box sits on the floor. It is too heavy to lift. What can you do? Push it! Get low. Put your hands on the box. Push with your legs. The box slides.
Still too heavy? Ask a friend. Two pushes are bigger than one. Or put the box on a cart. Wheels roll. A cart makes pushing easy.
A *ramp* helps too. A ramp is a flat slope. Push the box up the ramp. It is easier than lifting. Movers use ramps every day.

words.d: a flat slope that goes from low to high

look.title: The Moving Truck
look.text: A moving truck is parked on a street in Chicago. A long ramp goes from the ground to the truck. Two movers push a couch up the ramp. It rolls on a cart with wheels. Up it goes. No one has to lift the couch.
look.prompt: Why do the movers use a ramp and wheels?

check.q: A box is too heavy to lift. What can you try?
check.why: You do not have to lift it. A push can slide the box across the floor.

check.q: Two friends push together. What kind of push is that?
check.why: Two pushes are bigger than one. A bigger push moves a heavier box.

check.q: What does a ramp help you do?
choices: Move a box up without lifting it
check.why: A ramp is a slope. You push the box up it instead of lifting it.

review.why: A force is a push or a pull. Forces make things move, stop and turn.

review.q: A push moves a thing which way?
review.why: A push presses on a thing and sends it away from you.

review.q: You want a ball to go far. What push do you use?
review.why: A big push makes a big change. The hard push sends the ball far.

review.q: A ball rolls onto thick grass and stops. Why?
choices: The grass pushed on the ball
review.why: The grass rubs on the ball. That push slows it down until it stops.

review.q: A rolling ball bumps a still ball. What happens to the still ball?
review.why: Things that touch can push each other. The rolling ball pushes the still one.

review.q: A box is too heavy to lift into a truck. What helps most?
review.why: A ramp lets you push the box up instead of lifting it.
